summary: Radar for 2026-11-19. Two things are moving right now. (1) Foundayo (orforglipron) is spreading outside the US. Health Canada authorized it on Nov 13 (reported Nov 18), with pharmacy launch expected in January. Australian GPs can now prescribe it (RACGP, Nov 17–19), and NICE's UK decision was due Nov 18. Our Foundayo video is already the second-fastest earner (+49 min/day), so the queued label-only "what to expect" long video should ship next. (2) The Thanksgiving window peaks in 4–8 days. UCLA Health published GLP-1 holiday tips on Nov 18, so holiday-table Shorts and pen-travel Shorts should run every night until 11-27. One new broad searched question is building: "why doesn't it work for everyone?" ScienceDaily (Nov 19) adds to the Nature Metabolism GLP1R-variant study, and it makes a good broad "Tirzepatide (Mounjaro) not working?" long video. Health Canada's Mounjaro heart-risk approval in type 2 diabetes (SURPASS-CVOT, randomized against dulaglutide) is a solid benefits-beyond-weight hook. The NAION eye-warning story is still alive (Moran Eye Center and MedPage, Nov 18); fold it into the queued Serious Risks long video rather than making a standalone piece. SURMOUNT-ADOLESCENTS (JAMA) and STEP Young (NEJM) dominate the news, but they are about children and teens, and our audience is adults. Use them only as a cautious Short, if at all. Rejected: compounded-GLP-1 warning letters (sourcing guardrail), the psychosis-after-stopping case reports (n=2, fear bait), the 'GLP-1 vacation', employer coverage and pricing stories, the low-dose persistence data (dosing territory), and black-market retatrutide. Evergreen 'Is this normal?' Shorts (injection site, hair in women, nausea, pen blood) stay the base for the 08:00 slot. Verification notes: Health Canada's Foundayo authorization is confirmed by CTV and Global News. NICE's Nov 18 decision is confirmed only as scheduled; the outcome isn't verified. The Health Canada Mounjaro heart-risk approval comes from Lilly's PR Newswire Canada release (FDA equivalent August 2026). The Washington Post strength piece wasn't retrievable; cite T-REx and the label instead.

candidates.angle: Long video (queued #4): 'Tirzepatide's pill cousin? Foundayo: What to Expect', built from the label only. Cover who it's approved for (adults with obesity, or overweight plus a weight-related condition), how a daily pill differs from a weekly shot, common GI effects mostly during dose escalation, and the label's top-dose result (17.2 mg, −11.1%), kept separate from the 36 mg trial number. No amounts, no cost. Link to How It Works.

candidates.topic: Tirzepatide (Mounjaro) not working? Why results vary from person to person: trial spread, GLP1R gene variants, metabolism
candidates.angle: Broad long video: 'Tirzepatide (Mounjaro) Not Working? Why Results Vary'. Start with SURMOUNT-1's spread of results in the full trial population (some lose far more than average, some less). Then cover the Nature Metabolism genetics finding, which is an association: rare GLP1R variants blunted semaglutide loss (2.4% vs 8.9%) much more than tirzepatide (13.3% vs 15.2%). Add ScienceDaily's metabolism explainer, then questions to bring to your prescriber. No switching advice.

candidates.topic: Tirzepatide (Mounjaro) and your heart: SURPASS-CVOT head-to-head vs dulaglutide, now a heart-risk indication in Canada as well as the US (adults with type 2 diabetes and heart disease)
